Aga for State and Sri Akhilendra Yadav, Advocate for Informant.
2. Applicant-Khetpal alias Arun has approached this Court by way of filing present bail application
seeking enlargement on bail in Case Crime No. 418 of 2022, under Sections 376, 452, 504, 506 Ipc,
Police Station Jasrana, District Firozabad, after rejection of his bail application vide order dated
07.10.2022 passed by Sessions Judge, Firozabad.

sentences.text: 3.  In the present case victim is a married woman, aged out 20 years old, who lodged FIR herself against applicant and one unknown person that when she was alone on fateful day at her house (her husband normally remained outside the house in relation to work), applicant and co-accused entered at her house and both raped her.
Her three years old child was put under threat of life by putting a country made pistol on his head.

4. Learned counsel for applicant submits that alleged occurrence took place on 21.12.2021 whereas application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. was filed on 04.01.2022 with a delay of about two weeks Khetpal @ Arun vs State Of U.P. on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12978457/

sentences.text: and on the basis of order passed by Magistrate concerned, FIR was lodged on 17.08.2022 (with delay of more than seven months).

Victim?s statement recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
was contrary with regard to number of assailants.

In statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C.
she has levelled allegation against applicant only whereas in statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
she has added one more person.
However, after investigation charge sheet has been filed only against applicant, as such, victim?s narration of facts are false.
Medical examination has not supported prosecution case.
Victim has not made any attempt to lodged a prompt FIR.
Family of both parties were doing common business, however, later on some dispute arose and this was the reason that applicant has been falsely implicated.

5. Learned AGA appearing for State and learned counsel for Informant submit that FIR was lodged only after order of Magistrate passed on application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C. and said order was never challenged by applicant, therefore, submission of counsel for applicant about delay in lodging FIR has prima facie no legal consequence.
Statement of victim in FIR and under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. remained consistent with regard to allegation qua to applicant.
No advantage can be granted to applicant of false implication of second assailant and a fair investigation has been conducted as charge sheet is filed only against applicant.
Since medical examination was conducted after many months, therefore, it is obvious that it would not support case of prosecution.
6. LAW ON BAIL - A SUMMARY (A) The basic rule may perhaps be tersely put as bail, not jail.

(B) Power to grant bail under Section 439 Cr.P.C., is of wide amplitude but not an unfettered discretion, which calls for exercise in a judicious manner and not as a matter of course or in whimsical manner.

(C) While passing an order on an application for grant of bail, there is no need to record elaborate details to give an impression that the case is one that would result in a conviction or, by contrast, in an acquittal.

However, a Court cannot completely divorce its decision from material aspects of the case such as allegations made against accused; nature and gravity of accusation; having common object or intention; severity of punishment if allegations are proved beyond reasonable doubt and would result in a conviction; reasonable apprehension of witnesses being influenced by accused;
tampering of evidence; character, behaviour, means, position and standing of accused; likelihood of offence being repeated; the frivolity in the case of prosecution; criminal antecedents of accused and a prima facie satisfaction of Court in support of charge against accused.

The Court may also take note of participation or part of an unlawful assembly as well as that circumstantial evidence not being a ground to grant bail, if the evidence/ material collected establishes prima facie a complete chain of events.
Parity may not be an only ground but remains a relevant factor for consideration of application for bail.

(D) Over crowding of jail and gross delay in disposal of cases when undertrials are forced to remain in jail (not due to their fault) may give rise to possible situations that may justify invocation of Article 21 of Constitution, may also be considered along with other factors.

sentences.text: In the present case, FIR was lodged after the order was passed by Magistrate concerned on application filed by victim under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., therefore, delay, if any, would not be adverse to prosecution case.

There may be some exaggeration by victim by involving another assailant also, however, there is a merit in the argument of learned AGA and counsel for Informant that allegation qua to applicant remained consistent in FIR and in statement of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.

Since charge sheet has been filed only against applicant,
therefore, merely that allegations were not found true with regard to another assailant, entire prosecution story would not come under the cloud of doubt.

8. Considering that there are serious and grievous allegations against applicant, which have been corroborated by evidence of victim recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and that till date statement of victim has not been recorded during trial, therefore, no case of bail is made out and prayer for bail is rejected.

9. However, the application is disposed of with direction to Trial Court to record statement of victim, if not already recorded, within a period of three months from today, if there is no other legal impediment.
Thereafter applicant is at liberty to file fresh application for bail before Trial Court.
